subject: VitaCore private deployment — security posture recap & questionnaire
messages:
From: Danielle Moore <danielle@vitacorehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@vitacorehealth.com, procurement@vitacorehealth.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up from today — security items and next steps

Thanks for the call earlier, Marcus — that was helpful. Quick recap and asks from our side so we can move internal approval along:

- We need confirmation of Redwood's SOC 2 status and a redacted report we can share with our compliance team.
- Clarify HIPAA handling for PHI in private (VPC/on-prem) deployments — e.g., egress controls and KMS options.
- Can you share a simple network diagram for the private deployment (VPC + optional air-gapped site) we discussed?
- We'd like the vendor security questionnaire filled and returned so our GRC team can review (I'll attach).

Would you be able to provide the SOC 2 redacted report and a draft of the completed questionnaire by COB Tuesday PST? Also please flag any items that typically delay procurement so we can plan.

Thanks,
Danielle
Director, IT Security
VitaCore Therapeutics

Attachments: VitaCore_Security_Questionnaire_v1.pdf (18 KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Danielle Moore <danielle@vitacorehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:13:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — security items and next steps

Danielle — thanks for the clear list and for sharing the questionnaire. Short answers and next steps below, plus what we'll attach.

1) SOC 2: Redwood has an active SOC 2 Type II report covering our hosted and private control plane. We will provide a redacted version (PII removed) that you can share with GRC. Attached: SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-redacted.pdf.

2) HIPAA/PHI: For private/VPC deployments we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and network controls to keep egress minimized. Our standard pattern for PHI workloads is: private control plane, customer-managed KMS, strict outbound egress rules, and optional explicit air-gapped worker pools if required. We will document concrete controls below in the network diagram.

3) Network diagram: attaching a first-pass diagram (redwood-private-deploy-netdiag-v1.png). It includes VPC subnets, NAT/egress paths, optional on-prem airgapped workers, and KMS integration points. This is a draft — happy to iterate.

4) Questionnaire: we'll start filling the VitaCore questionnaire and return a completed copy by EOD Tuesday PST (we may have a couple of follow-ups on clarifications).

Potential procurement blockers (to be aware of):
- Desired data residency or explicit air-gap requirements requiring an on-prem footprint — adds lead time for infra setup.
- Encryption attestations beyond KMS integration (we can provide architecture and key lifecycle docs, but FIPS/HSM proofs depend on your KMS vendor).
- Long-tail indemnity or data processing clauses in the contract — we can discuss standard enterprise terms.

Next steps:
- Laura will own the SOC/attestations and questionnaire responses.
- Ethan will scope a hardened deployment diagram and list configuration knobs (egress ACLs, host-level hardening).
- I'll follow up with a proposed date for a technical walkthrough next week.

Marcus Lin
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-redacted.pdf, redwood-private-deploy-netdiag-v1.png

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Danielle Moore <danielle@vitacorehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — security items and next steps

Hi Danielle — following up on Marcus' note. We're working through the questionnaire and have a few clarifying points where your team input would shorten the back-and-forth:

A) Question 4.2 requests details on key rotation frequency — do you require a specific rotation cadence (e.g., 90 days) or is standard KMS-managed rotation acceptable?
B) Question 7.1 asks whether we can support isolated worker pools that never have outbound internet access; we can, but need to confirm whether VitaCore would manage software updates locally or accept scheduled maintenance windows to sync updates via an approved bastion.

If you can drop a quick note on the above two items we will finalize and return the questionnaire. If useful, we can also accept a short call with your GRC lead to walk through the answers.

Warmly,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Security | Redwood Inference

From: security@vitacorehealth.com <security@vitacorehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Danielle Moore <danielle@vitacorehealth.com>, procurement@vitacorehealth.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — security items and next steps

Laura — good questions. Quick answers from VitaCore's GRC: 

1) Key rotation: default 90 days for any keys that protect PHI.
2) Isolated worker pools: VitaCore prefers worker pools with no outbound internet. We can provide a signed maintenance policy for update windows and will expect an approved bastion pattern for package syncs.

We'll accept the redacted SOC 2 and the network diagram you shared; procurement will need the completed questionnaire and an initial statement of costs for a private deployment (rough order of magnitude).

Danielle
On behalf of VitaCore GRC
